chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from al-Minqari, from Ali ibn Hashim ibn al-Barid, from his father, who said:

A man came to Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) and asked him about certain matters, and he answered. Then the man returned to ask about similar matters. So Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) said:

It is written in the Injil (Gospel): 'Do not seek knowledge of what you do not know while you have not yet acted upon what you already know, for indeed knowledge, when not acted upon, does not increase its owner except in disbelief, and does not increase him from God except in remoteness.'

key_terms.الْإِنْجِيلِ: The Injil (Gospel) — the original divine scripture revealed to Prophet Isa (Jesus, AS). In Islamic tradition, it is believed to have been a genuine revelation that was later altered. Here, Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) cites it as an authoritative source shared across Abrahamic traditions.
key_terms.بُعْداً: Bu'd (remoteness/distance) — spiritual distance from God resulting from failure to act on one's knowledge.
key_terms.كُفْراً: Kufr — often translated as disbelief or ingratitude. In this context, it refers to ingratitude for the blessing of knowledge — possessing knowledge and neglecting to act upon it is a form of ungratefulness toward God.

ai.seo_question: What did Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS) say about seeking more knowledge without acting on what you already know?
ai.summary: Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS), the fourth Imam known as Zayn al-Abidin, rebukes a man who repeatedly sought more knowledge without implementing what he already knew, citing a teaching from the Injil (Gospel). The teaching encapsulates a profound principle: knowledge without action is spiritually harmful, leading not to growth in faith but to greater ingratitude and distance from God. This hadith belongs to a broader chapter on the obligation of utilizing knowledge, reflecting the Shia scholarly tradition that actionable knowledge — knowledge that transforms behavior — is the true purpose of learning.
